docs.title: go-ruby-reline documentation
docs.text:
Pure-Go, MRI-4.0.5-faithful Ruby reline (no cgo)

go-ruby-reline/reline is a faithful, pure-Go (zero cgo) reimplementation of Ruby's reline, matching reference Ruby (MRI) behaviour. The module path is github.com/go-ruby-reline/reline.

It is a standalone, reusable library importable by any Go program, and the backend bound into go-embedded-ruby by rbgo as a native module — the same pattern as go-ruby-yaml. The dependency runs the other way: this library has no dependency on the Ruby runtime.

Status: pure-Go, CGO=0, differential-tested

A faithful pure-Go port of Ruby's reline, validated against reference Ruby, at 100% coverage, gofmt + go vet clean, CI green across the six 64-bit Go targets and three OSes.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
• Pure Go, CGO_ENABLED=0 — trivial cross-compilation, a single static binary, no C toolchain.
  • Reference-faithful. Behaviour matches reference Ruby (MRI), validated by a differential oracle rather than approximated.
  • Standalone & reusable. No dependency on the Ruby runtime — the dependency runs the other way; rbgo binds this module.
  • 100% test coverage is the target, enforced as a CI gate, across 6 arches.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Why pure Go — why this slice of Ruby lives as a standalone, interpreter-independent Go library.
  • Reference — install, import path and the API reference.
  • Terminal host — ReadKeys, the ANSI key bindings and the terminal package, a line editor on a real terminal (v0.1.0).

Source lives at github.com/go-ruby-reline/reline.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Contributions are welcome. go-ruby-reline/reline is built to a small set of non-negotiable rules — they keep it pure-Go, correct, and reference-faithful.

docs.title: Hard rules
docs.text:
• Build from source — no vendoring. Everything compiles from source.
  • 100% test coverage target, enforced in CI. New code ships with tests, and coverage is a CI gate. Fill the error branches, not just the happy path.
  • All GitHub content in English. Issues, pull requests, commits and comments are English-only.
  • Differential testing against reference Ruby. Correctness is defined by reference Ruby (MRI), compared rather than approximated from memory.
  • Pure Go, cgo disabled. The whole point is a single static binary with no C toolchain. Code must build with CGO_ENABLED=0.
  • A reusable library, not the interpreter. Anything that needs a live Ruby binding belongs in the consumer (rbgo), not here.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Pick or open an issue describing the change.
  2. Work test-first: add the differential / unit tests, then make them pass.

  3. Run the full suite with coverage and confirm the gate is green:

    COVERPKG=$(go list ./... | paste -sd, -)
go test -race -coverpkg="$COVERPKG" -coverprofile=cover.out ./...
go tool cover -func=cover.out | tail -1   # 100.0%

  4. Open a PR in English, referencing the issue.

docs.text: The public API lives at the module root (github.com/go-ruby-reline/reline). It is Ruby-shaped but Go-idiomatic: names mirror Ruby's reline, while the surface follows Go conventions — value types, explicit errors, no global state.

docs.text:

The module's README carries worked examples and the full, up-to-date surface. This page intentionally links to those canonical sources rather than duplicating signatures that could drift out of date.

docs.title: Conformance
docs.text: Behaviour is pinned by a differential oracle against reference Ruby: a corpus is run through both the ruby binary and this library and the results are compared, gated on the reference where relevant and skipping itself where ruby is absent so the cross-arch lanes still validate the library.

docs.title: Terminal host
docs.text:
Since v0.1.0

The host pieces and the terminal package arrive in v0.1.0.

The editing core is pure: it needs no interpreter and no tty. Everything that touches a real terminal sits behind the reline.IO interface (GetC, UngetC, GetScreenSize, Write, MoveCursorColumn, EraseAfterCursor, ClearScreen). A NullIO (fixed 24×80, recording) ships for tests and headless use.

docs.title: Host pieces in the root package
docs.text:
The host-side parts of MRI that are still pure Go live in github.com/go-ruby-reline/reline:

API Port of ReadKeys(config, io) Reline::Core#read_io: bytes to keys through the keymap, with the keyseq-timeout wait on a lone ESC SetANSIKeyBindings(config) Reline::ANSI#set_default_key_bindings: cursor keys in CSI and SS3 form, Ctrl/Meta arrows, Delete, Home/End, Page Up/Down, Shift-Tab, M-space, C-x C-x, bracketed paste start Config.AddDefaultKeyBinding the default key-binding table behind the ANSI bindings key_delete the Delete command MenuLines(list, width) MenuInfo#lines: the completion menu's columns LineEditor.TakeMenu() hands the pending completion menu to the host

The root package imports neither golang.org/x/term nor golang.org/x/sys.

docs.title: On a real terminal: terminal
docs.text:
import "github.com/go-ruby-reline/reline/terminal"

The terminal package is the IO seam, wired: a reline.IO on a real terminal (raw mode and window size through golang.org/x/term; virtual-terminal output enabled on the Windows console). It puts the terminal in raw mode for one read, decodes the keys, drives the LineEditor, and redraws the edited lines, their prompts and the completion menu after every key (MRI Reline.readline / Reline.readmultiline over Reline::ANSI).

It supports multiline reads with a termination predicate, per-line prompts, Tab completion with the menu drawn below the line, history, bracketed paste and Ctrl-L. It runs on Linux, macOS and Windows 10+. The module requires golang.org/x/term and golang.org/x/sys.

t := terminal.New(os.Stdin, os.Stdout) // os.Stdin must be a terminal
for {
    line, err := t.Readline(terminal.Options{
        Prompt:     "> ",
        Terminate:  complete,     // multiline: Enter submits when this accepts the buffer
        Complete:   candidates,   // Tab
        AddHistory: true,
    })
    if err == io.EOF { break }                 // Ctrl-D on an empty line
    if errors.Is(err, terminal.ErrInterrupt) { continue } // Ctrl-C
    run(line)
}

terminal.Options has the fields Prompt, Terminate, PromptProc, Complete, AppendCharacter and AddHistory. Readline returns io.EOF on Ctrl-D or end of input, and terminal.ErrInterrupt on Ctrl-C.

Between two reads the terminal is back in its normal mode, so a program's own output needs no care. go-notebook's notebook irb is built on it.

docs.title: Why pure Go
docs.text: go-ruby-reline/reline reimplements Ruby's reline in pure Go, with cgo disabled. The slice of Ruby it covers is deterministic and interpreter-independent: given its inputs, the result is a pure function of those inputs — no live binding, no evaluation of arbitrary Ruby. That is exactly the part that can — and should — live as a standalone Go library, separate from the interpreter.

docs.title: Extracted for reuse, reusable by anyone
docs.text:
• any Go program can import github.com/go-ruby-reline/reline directly, with no Ruby runtime;
  • the dependency runs the other way — rbgo binds this module as a native module for go-embedded-ruby (the same pattern as go-ruby-yaml), rather than this module depending on the interpreter;
  • the behaviour is pinned by a differential oracle against reference Ruby, independent of any one consumer.

docs.title: Why pure Go matters here
docs.text:
Because the library is CGO-free, it:

  • cross-compiles to every Go target with no C toolchain, and links into a single static binary;
  • has no dependency on the Ruby runtime — the dependency runs the other way;
  • can be differentially tested against the ruby binary wherever one is on PATH, while the cross-arch lanes still validate the library itself.

See Reference for the import path and API.
